text.p: These are the leading stories in Zimbabwe's state-owned Herald newspaper on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Developed countries on Sunday came under fire from members of the Group of 15 (G-15) developing countries meeting in Zimbabwe for using "strong arm" tactics to force developing countries into international trade agreements that in the end compromise national sovereignty.

- Senegalese Prime Minister Habib Thiam, attending the sixth G-15 summit in Harare said on Sunday members of the grouping should increase trade among themselves, saying at the moment they trade more with the developed world.

- Argentine vice-president Carlos Ruckauf said at the opening of the sixth G-15 summit on Sunday a working programme should be settled at the next ministerial meeting of the grouping to remove all trade distortions imposed on agricultural sectors of developing nations by industrialised countries.
